title: I made a strategy game in one weekend with AI and now me and my friends play it every day
author: Embarrassed_Steak309
selftext:
Hi guys, last weekend I made Ten Moons, a turn based multiplayer strategy game in the browser where you found cities, make armies, cross the sea with ships and if you take the enemy capital you win. 

I made it because on friday night me and my friends wanted to play a strategy game together. We tried some of them on mobile, but nothing convinced us because there were very few free online options.   
  
So that night I said: ok, let's try to make my own  
.  
Here is the link: [playtenmoons.com](https://playtenmoons.com/)

I made the first raw version in 1 hour than we end up playing until 4am and in the weekend I improved it a lot and made it way more fun and balanced.

I did everything with Claude code and all the 3D is made by code with three.js, it's a browser game and you can play from both mobile and desktop. And right now it's completely free to play you don't even need an account.

Two days ago I posted it on reddit and I got 15k views and 90 upvotes on r/playmygame, and me and my friends are playing everyday. I also reached 100 people that played the game.  
  
Now I start questioning what to do with it, do you have any idea?

I mean how can I improve it further? Could I make some bucks with it?

comments.author: Commercial-Ad9859
comments.body:
The fact that you and your friends are still playing it every day is probably the most valuable feedback you could have received.  
I’m also a solo developer working extensively with Claude Code, and I think one of the biggest challenges with AI-assisted game development is knowing when to stop building and start refining.  
You already have something that people genuinely want to play. Don’t underestimate that.  
I wouldn’t rush into monetization or adding hundreds of features. Build a small community around the game, listen to your returning players and figure out what keeps them coming back.  
The ability to create a game in a weekend is impressive, but creating something people still want to play six months later is where the real achievement lies.  
Keep going. You’ve got a genuinely interesting starting point.

replies.author: counterclockwisdom
replies.body:
Well, what compels you and your friends to play it excessively? Polish how well the game gives you the experience you crave. If the part you like is pondering deep strategy from simple parts, try to make it better without overcomplicating. Consider alternate behaviors/mechanics/rules that might add depth or make scenarios more interesting, add a new mechanic or tile type, etc., as long as it makes the game more enticing rather than less.

Also think about reducing friction if you ever get a feeling of wanting to play the game but start to dread a part of the experience.

replies.author: Embarrassed_Steak309

Yes the thing that we like is the competitive aspect of the game where the smartest player is able to win. Thank you for your reply I will think about it in the next days.

Play it give me a lot of ideas so let’s see in the next matches what will happen

replies.author: counterclockwisdom
replies.body: I would try it, but I don’t enjoy civilization strategy games, so my feedback for polishing the core loop into something you crave will not be nearly as useful as yours and your friends’.

replies.author: Embarrassed_Steak309
replies.body:
I understand that few people like turn based games. What genre do you like?

While reading your reply I had the idea of trying to do something like StarCraft, age of empire or command&conquer next. I am not sure if I am be able to do it but I wanna try

replies.author: counterclockwisdom
replies.body:
I like less competitive games and more social or RPG games, like Hollow Knight or REPO or Stardew Valley. I also really like puzzle and strategy and strategy roguelites.

I did enjoy the Starcraft II campaign. PvE RTS games seem to be in a short supply right now compared to all the attempts at making PvP RTS. RTS in general is really hard to design and balance, though, so I wouldn’t recommend an RTS as a casual project unless you’re making a bite-sized one or are really dedicated to designing a good RTS.

comments.author: golfstreamer
comments.body: Why are people obsessed with short time lines? The code may have been written in a weekend but the gameplay (the most important part of a game) was definitely not. Why do you need to brag about these impossible timescales?

replies.author: Embarrassed_Steak309

replies.author: golfstreamer

replies.author: Embarrassed_Steak309
replies.body: ![gif](giphy|LyJ6KPlrFdKnK)

replies.author: golfstreamer
replies.body: As I said. It looked to  me that a lot of thought went into this game. When you say things like "It's inspired by Civilization / Polytopoia" I got the impression that you spent quite some time thinking about how this game should work. The two days would just be the final implementation of this deeper thought processes. But you seem to insist that you actually put very little thought into it.

replies.author: Embarrassed_Steak309

replies.author: golfstreamer
replies.body:
Ah, that explains it. I guess then you do have a good background for this. 

I don't know I guess these posts where people give these super short time scales don't sit right with me. I just feel like it gives people the wrong impression. Like can average person who isn't as knowledable as you do this? 

I might be being too sensitive. But I feel for the guys who look at posts like this thinking "This guy made a good game in two days and it's taking me weeks / months. Am I an idiot?".

replies.author: Embarrassed_Steak309

Nah I don’t think the average person is able to do it. I work with AI everyday so that’s different from someone that just try AI for the first time and I made a lot of projects in the last 3 years.

I don’t write complex prompt but I learned how to think and control my ideas and brainstorm with the machine as well
